sections.content:
5,520 people

were counted on the census as "pest control officers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Pest control officers investigate the presence of pests that are hazardous to public health or cause nuisance, (such as rats), lay traps to capture pests and treat areas of infestation.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "pest control officers" there were more men than women (93.6% compared with 6.4%).

This means "pest control officers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 93.7% and women made up 6.3% of "pest control officers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "pest control officers" included:

  • telecoms and related network installers and repairers
  • electrical and electronic trades (other)
  • street cleaners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "pest control officers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "pest control officers", 15.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "pest control officers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "pest control officers" included:

  • assemblers (electrical and electronic products)
  • mobile machine drivers and operatives (other)
  • construction operatives (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "pest control officers", 11.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (80.9% compared with 19.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (66.8%) than self-employed (33.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
